results.fact: Whether trailhead parking requires a fee/pass
results.correct_value: No parking pass at the crag's unofficial roadside pulloff
results.evidence: The crag is reached from an unofficial roadside pulloff uphill of the double hairpin on the Old Stevens Pass Highway (~1.4 mi from US-2), with no developed parking or facilities. Federal recreation-fee law bars standard-amenity fees 'solely for parking, undesignated parking, or picnicking along roads or trailsides' and allows them only where there is developed parking, a toilet, trash, an information kiosk, picnic tables and security; the national forest's own pass page says passes are required at many developed trailheads and that fee sites are signed; a statewide pass FAQ says the pass is only required where the trailhead offers developed facilities. So no pass is needed at the pulloff (the Wellington fee trailhead is a different site 2.8 mi up the road). access.passRequired is set to agree with access.notes/parking_pass; `permit`'s 'Northwest Forest Pass at developed trailheads' is already conditional and stays.

patches.value: None at the crag's roadside pulloff (not a fee site)

results.evidence: Third pass. Re-measured with the Forest Service wilderness boundary layer (with geometry): the crag pin lies OUTSIDE any wilderness, 165 m south of the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness boundary, and the ground height at the pin (4,758 ft, USGS 1 m DEM) fits the approach described for the crag (about 1,000 ft of gain from the hairpin pulloff), while the boundary point 165 m north is already at ~5,230 ft. Wild Sky Wilderness is more than 4 km away, so the Wild Sky name is certainly wrong. But no source states the crag's wilderness status or permit rule, and a 165 m margin is within the uncertainty of a guidebook-database pin, so the replacement text (no permit vs. a Henry M. Jackson self-issue permit) is still not settled; nothing patched. Suggested owner fix: drop the Wild Sky clause from `permit` so it agrees with access.permit 'N/A'.

results.correct_value: Class 2-3 for Hurry-up Peak; the Class 3-4 text belongs to Magic Mountain
results.evidence: STRUCTURAL: the Class 3-4 wording is Magic Mountain's route, not Hurry-up's. A club route page titled Magic Mountain/South Ridge (archived) reads: from Kool-Aid Lake ascend 1,000 ft to the col between Magic Mountain and Hurry Up Peak, gain the south ridge to the false summit, drop 80 ft into a dirty gully and take Class 3-4 ledges that corkscrew the east side of the summit; the archived traverse stage page confirms the standard route up Magic is its S ridge starting near Kool-Aid Lake; and OpenStreetMap puts Magic Mountain (48.4456,-121.0411) 1.3 km NORTH of Hurry-up (48.4339,-121.0380), so a south ridge rising from that col leads to Magic. pitch_detail rows 2-3 (col to false summit, 80-ft gully, corkscrew) and the summit waypoint's directions copy that text almost word for word, and they are what carry 'Class 3-4' into grade. Sources for Hurry-up itself give class 3 (encyclopedia) and class 2-3 with moderate exposure on the summit ridge (a traverse trip report), matching rock_grade and climbing_route. Owner fix: clear or rewrite pitch_detail rows 2-3 and the summit waypoint directions for Hurry-up's own line, then set grade to 'Grade II, Class 2-3'.
